boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the African Brigade and the 23rd Iowa, and McCulloch's Brigade, without counts; the live field reads zero. Dennis reports the Union force at 1,061 and the Confederates at one brigade of about 2,500 with 200 cavalry. McCulloch says his full strength on the field did not exceed 1,500 and the enemy's must have been twice, if not three times, that.
claims.rationale: Each commander's count of his own force differs from his opponent's estimate; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Dennis says Lieb's reconnaissance on June 6 met Confederate pickets and a pursuing force and that Lieb sent word the enemy was advancing, after which Dennis sent the 23rd Iowa and Porter the Choctaw. McCulloch says Taylor's orders assumed only a cavalry battalion and a Black infantry battalion without guns or gunboats, while he believes the defenders were fully apprised and reinforced by three transport loads overnight.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge in the two opposing reports; McCulloch's belief about Union warning is his inference.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS and Dennis say the fighting continued until about noon, when the Confederates withdrew under fire from the pursuing troops and the gunboats. McCulloch writes that only the best fighting could have given his brigade even partial success.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. McCulloch's characterization is attributed and not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 837 total (US 652; CS 185). Dennis gives Union losses of 652, footnoted as 101 killed, 285 wounded and 266 captured or missing, and estimates the Confederate loss at about 150 killed and 300 wounded. McCulloch reports 44 killed, 130 wounded and 10 missing, 184 in all (his return table prints 185), and puts the Union loss at over a thousand.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Each side's estimate of the other's loss is far above the other's own count; neither estimate is adopted. The footnote's categories are summed here (11+90, 17+268, 2+264).

open_questions: Taylor's, Walker's, Hawes's and Porter's reports, the Union regimental reports and the treatment of captured Black soldiers remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
